cards.def: Halfdane had four children, Heorogar, Hrothgar, Halga, and a daughter who became the queen of the Swede Onela.
On his first night in Heorot, Grendel seized thirty sleeping men and carried them back to his lair.
Grendel struck again just one night after his first raid, which showed the Danes that his attacks would not stop.
Grendel terrorized Heorot for twelve winters, long enough for news of Hrothgar's sorrow to spread across the world.
Beowulf sailed with fourteen hand-picked companions, making a band of fifteen Geats.

cards.term: The second day of the voyage
cards.def: The Geats sighted the Danish cliffs on the day after they set sail, after an easy crossing on a calm sea.
Sailors reported that Beowulf had the strength of thirty men in the grip of each hand, which is why Hrothgar hopes he can beat Grendel.
Beowulf boasts that he once battled and bound five beasts, part of the record that convinced the Geat elders to send him.
Unferth claims that Beowulf and Breca struggled in the sea for seven nights before Breca won.
Beowulf says that he and Breca swam side by side for five nights until storms drove them apart.
Beowulf says his sword killed nine sea monsters during the swim, which made the sea safe for sailors.
Grendel devoured one sleeping Geat before reaching for Beowulf, and Hrothgar later paid gold as compensation for him.
After Grendel's defeat, Hrothgar gave Beowulf four treasures, a golden standard, a mail shirt, a helmet, and a sword.
Hrothgar also gave Beowulf eight horses with gold bridles, one of them carrying Hrothgar's own battle-saddle.
Wealhtheow gave Beowulf two arm bangles, a mail shirt, rings, and the finest gold torque the poet had ever heard of.
Beowulf is about 3,182 lines long in the original Old English, which makes it the longest surviving epic in Old English.
The only surviving manuscript of Beowulf was copied by two scribes around the year 1000.
Beowulf was perhaps composed around 750, but scholars still debate a date anywhere from the 700s to about 1000.
In 1731 a fire in the Cotton library scorched the Beowulf manuscript, which is why some of its lines are now damaged or lost.
Cotton Vitellius A.xv is the British Library catalogue name for the single manuscript that preserves Beowulf.
Seamus Heaney's translation of Beowulf was published in 1999.
